title: Tenant channel mapping and upgrade lifecycle playbook
body:
Purpose and audience

This working playbook defines a tenant-focused notification lifecycle, channel mapping, and sample message templates for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) upgrade windows and SLA-impacting maintenance. Intended audience: engineering on-call, program managers, account owners, and customer success managers owning private deployments.

High level goals
- Make notices predictable and scannable: what changes, impact, required customer action, rollback plan.
- Map each tenant to primary + fallback communication channels.
- Provide short, medium, and long-form templates for e-mail, product banner, and support portal entries.
- Capture minimal Terraform module notes that reduce churn during upgrades (upgrade flags, compatibility checks).

Quick glossary
- Tenant: customer instance of Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem).
- Owner: Redwood AM / CSM tied to tenant.
- Primary channel: the channel we will use first (email or support portal).
- Secondary channel: Slack/Teams, or Pager duty for urgent incidents.

Channel mapping matrix (how we pick channels)
- Scheduled maintenance (non-SLA affecting): Primary = support portal notice + email to technical contact; Secondary = workspace Slack/Teams message.
- Rolling upgrades with potential transient latency: Primary = email + product banner; Secondary = CSM Slack/Teams.
- SLA-impacting maintenance or potential downtime: Primary = email + SMS to emergency contact (if configured); Secondary = phone call from AM, and incident page link.
- Urgent unplanned incidents: Primary = PagerDuty -> phone escalation; Secondary = incident page + email summary.

How to assemble the recipient list (notes to on-call)
1) Query tenant metadata from the control plane: technical_contact_emails, billing_contact, emergency_contact_phone, slack_workspace_id (if provided), preferred_communication (email|slack|phone).
2) If preferred_communication is set, honor it. If not present, fallback to technical_contact_emails.
3) CSM must review list 72h before any SLA-impacting maintenance. If CSM flags an alternate contact, update the table.

Notification cadence (recommended)
- T-14 days: Heads-up email (informational). Include impact summary and optional dry-run window.
- T-7 days: Reminder email + support portal entry. Short bullet list of customer expected actions.
- T-48 hours: Technical preflight checklist to tenant: config snapshot, backup confirmation, contact window. Include scheduled start time in tenant timezone.
- T-2 hours: Final reminder (email + product banner) with rollback window and expected duration.
- During: Live incident/upgrade page link shared to primary channel; incremental updates every 30-60 min for long operations.
- Post-upgrade (T+0 to T+48 hours): Results summary email and optional customer satisfaction/check-in from CSM.

Templates (keeps them short and modular)
1) T-14 heads-up (Email subject): Planned maintenance window for your Redwood Private deployment
Body:
Hi <customer_name>,

We're planning a maintenance window for your Redwood Private environment hosted in <region>. This maintenance is part of a rolling platform upgrade that improves reliability and reduces tail-latency.

Planned start: <start_time> (<tenant_timezone>)
Estimated duration: ~<expected_duration>
Impact: <impact_summary> (e.g., no downtime expected / brief API interruptions / possible <minutes> of degraded throughput)
Action required: <any actions or none>

If you have concerns or a blackout period, please reply to this message within 5 business days or contact your CSM, <csm_name> (<csm_email>).

Thanks,
The Redwood Private Ops Team

2) T-48 technical preflight (Email subject): Preflight checklist for your upcoming maintenance on <date>
Body:
Hi <contact_name>,

As part of the upcoming maintenance on <date>, please confirm the following before we begin: 
- Backup/replication status: snapshot taken and verified (yes/no)
- Telemetry access: we can reach your telemetry endpoints (yes/no)
- Access window: on-call engineer available at start time (yes/no)

If any item is ‘no’, reply with the blocker and our SRE will follow up.

If you prefer a dry run, we can schedule one within the next 7 days.

3) Emergency / SLA-impacting notice (Email subject): Immediate outage affecting your Redwood Private deployment
Body:
Hi <customer_name>,

We are investigating an incident affecting your deployment in <region>. Current impact: <summary>. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation and will post updates every <interval> minutes here: <incident_page_url>.

Primary contact during incident: <on_call_name> (<on_call_phone>)
Estimated time to next update: <minutes>

We apologize for the disruption.

— Redwood SRE

Product banner copy (short)
- Upgrading platform components. Expect intermittent latency. See status: <incident_page_url>
- Maintenance in progress: read more in your inbox or contact your CSM.

Support portal / ticket template (short)
Title: Scheduled maintenance – <tenant_id> – <start_date>
Description:
Summary: Rolling upgrade for platform components. Start <start_time> • Est. <expected_duration> • Impact: <impact_summary>
Actions for tenant: confirm backup, confirm access window, monitor application.

Terraform module notes (concise, ops-focused)
- Module versioning: Add a required_version pin in the module usage to avoid surprise major bumps. Example: required_version = ">= 2.3.0, < 3.0.0".
- Feature flags: Expose an explicit variable for the upgrade-compatibility-mode (defaults to false). During canary upgrades set upgrade_compatibility_mode = true to enable tolerant behavior.
- Immutable tags: Add outputs that export the deployed module tag/version for audit and rollback reference. (module.deploy_tag)
- Migration steps: Provide a small tf plan script that validates no breaking changes: terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars -target=module.network -out=preflight.plan
- Drift checks: Recommend a preflight script that runs terraform state list and compares to last-known state snapshot.

Checklist for kernel/agent upgrades (notes to kernel team)
- Confirm KV cache persistence across agent restarts in canary cluster.
- Ensure sequence length and batching tests pass on small and large prompts.
- Smoke test generator against saved prompt harness (seeded randomness off).
- Verify logging and trace propagation to telemetry endpoints configured by tenant.

Rollback and what to tell customers
- We aim for fast rollback paths. Template customer message if rolling back: 
Subject: Rollback completed for maintenance on <date>
Body:
Hi <customer_name>,

We rolled back the recent changes for your environment due to <reason>. Normal service has been restored. Impact during rollback: <impact_summary>. We will follow up with a root cause timeline within 48 hours.

Next steps: a follow-up call is scheduled for <date> to discuss mitigations and a revised upgrade window.

Operational play notes (internal)
- Publish support portal notice as "private" so tenants see it in their dashboard experience and it sends email.
- Tag tickets with component:private-upgrade and severity (SEV-INFO/SEV-1 if SLA affected).
- Use incident page template: include runbook link (internal) and CSM contact.
- CSM should call any Tier 1 customers 24–72h before start for alignment.

Risk zones and mitigations
- Network egress blocks from tenant side: ask customers to run break-glass connectivity test 7 days prior.
- Custom firewall rules for agent telemetry: include short debug script in preflight mail to confirm endpoints.
- Terraform module incompatibility: maintain a compatibility table in the module README and run a compatibility CI job against a snapshot of common tenant environments.

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- Add an automated SMS opt-in step in the customer portal for emergency contact numbers. (owner: Maya)
- Build an API endpoint /internal/tenant-comm-preflight to programmatically fetch contact lists and preferred channels. (owner: Jonas)
- Create a short one-page CSM checklist for talking points during the T-72h call. (owner: Diego)

Appendix: sample preflight command snippets (for internal SRE)
- fetch tenant meta: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/<tenant_id>/meta
- run tf plan: cd infra/tenants/<tenant_id> && terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars -out=preflight.plan
- snapshot state: terraform state pull > state-<tenant_id>-<date>.json

Notes to self (tone: quick)
- Keep templates short — customers skim.
- Avoid alarmist language for non-SLA windows.
- Always include an explicit rollback sentence and who to call.

End of draft.
